name: Common envelope
blurb: A 0.5 solar mass main-sequence star, as a point mass, starts on a circular orbit just outside the surface of a 1 solar mass red giant of 50 solar radii (a 0.4 solar mass point-mass core in a convective envelope), and spirals into its envelope. The gas is hydrogen and helium with the tabulated equation of state: a red giant’s envelope is between 10⁴ and a few 10⁵ K, where both are partly ionized, and the energy their recombination gives back as the envelope expands is a large part of what binds it. Gas alone, without the radiation term. In the frame of the center of mass.
